profile.about:
I’m a customer-facing AI solutions architect and hands-on engineer who enjoys turning real business challenges into practical solutions. I work alongside customers and engineering teams from the first conversation through discovery, architecture, building, testing and delivery.

I bring together AI and agentic workflows, enterprise data integration and multi-cloud engineering, using technologies such as RAG, AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, DevOps and MLOps. What matters most to me is finding the right solution for the people who will use it.

Some of my work includes:

- **AI for the People:** Built an agent platform to help customers explore AI use cases and onboard to Rackspace’s GPU-for-rent offering.
- **YES AI CAN:** Built an internal “customer zero” platform where teams can develop and demonstrate reusable AI capabilities.
- **Banking AI agents:** Built a credit and asset appraisal POC designed to make reviews faster and more effective while keeping human decision-makers in control.
- **Supply Chain AI Manager:** Designed an AI solution for a major cosmetics company to support inventory planning and improve logistics speed and costs.
- **Gameloft:** Improved production cloud and data operations, helping reduce cloud spending by approximately US$40,000 per month.

In all my projects, I listen to people, understand their pain points and help them build, together, a realistic solution that makes their work easier, faster and more efficient, with better results. This is my passion and my mission. It is what I love to do: not just building products, but building real solutions for human endeavours.

projects.summary: An AI treasury agent investigates supplier invoices inside a system where it has no authority to move money: policy decides, humans approve, and a blockchain makes the audit record tamper-evident.

projects.title: KATS — KT AI Enhanced Ticket Support System
projects.subtitle: AI troubleshooting built on Kepner-Tregoe problem analysis
projects.status_note: Proof of concept. The built-in browser agent is a mock; an optional local RAG backend answers from the real ticket base, and nothing leaves the machine.
projects.summary: A support-ticket workflow built on a 10-step troubleshooting action plan rooted in Kepner-Tregoe problem analysis, with an AI agent that finds the shortest path to resolution from the knowledge base, customer history and problem register.
projects.problem: Ticket tools record what happened to a ticket, but rarely what the problem was — so the same issue is solved again and again, repeat customer issues go unnoticed and engineers duplicate work on the same outage.
projects.implementation:
- Universal Troubleshooting Action Plan: a 10-step method based on Kepner-Tregoe problem analysis
- AI agent that reads the knowledge base, customer history and problem register — including telling you when not to troubleshoot at all
- Runs offline in the browser from a single file
- Optional RAG backend: PostgreSQL/pgvector, a retrieval API and a local LLM

projects.title: MLM — Meaning Language Model
projects.subtitle: Understand meaning before predicting language
projects.status_note: Research proof of concept. Every claim is measured on identical input, and the cost is reported next to the benefit.
projects.summary: A research POC that asks what is happening, who is involved and what information is missing — then scores a Transformer's next-token candidates against that structure.
projects.problem: A conventional language model only asks which token statistically comes next. MLM tests whether first understanding meaning — roles, places, time — makes predictions better, and measures the cost honestly.
projects.role: Designed and built the research prototype.
projects.implementation:
- Pipeline: language, lexicon, grammar, morphology and syntax → Universal Phrase DNA → context graph → expected semantic slot → linguistic scoring of the Transformer's candidates
- Every component can be switched off for fair comparison on the same model and hardware
- Language packs, multimodal input (text, image, video) and AWS EC2 deployment

projects.title: ACM — Actions Consequential Model
projects.subtitle: See what an action changes before taking it
projects.context: Personal research project · builds on MLM
projects.summary: Built on the Meaning Language Model, ACM predicts what an action does: its consequences for the actor, for those it affects and for other actors’ goals — across a blast radius from the place it happens out to society and the earth.
projects.problem: AI agents are starting to take actions. Before acting, a system should be able to trace who and what an action will affect — including its own planned actions.
projects.role: Designed and built the research prototype.
projects.implementation:
- Uses MLM’s Universal Phrase DNA (who does what, to whom, where, when, how and why)
- Builds a graph of the full action in context and predicts consequences circle by circle
- Blast-radius layers: site, neighbours, organization, city, country, society and earth
- Stores every node as a vector to compare with past actions

architectures.title: Banking AI Copilot Platform — Agentic Credit Appraisal (Hybrid OpenStack + AWS)
architectures.summary: Full-stack target design for an enterprise banking copilot: SSO and RBAC, Flowise Agentflow V2 agents behind an MCP tool gateway, durable workflows, private LLM inference, GitLab MLOps and AWS staging.
architectures.description:
- Application layer: React/TypeScript analyst workspace, FastAPI + Pydantic backend, API gateway with OAuth2/OIDC single sign-on (Keycloak), RBAC, tenant isolation and audit logging.
- AI orchestration: Flowise Agentflow V2 with credit-scoring, asset-appraisal, legal/policy and fraud/AML agents; an MCP tool gateway; private LLM inference (Llama / Mistral) on OpenStack; RAG with PostgreSQL + pgvector and Neo4j; connectors for Temenos core banking, ERP/CRM, REST, SFTP and email.
- Workflow & execution: Temporal for durable, long-running workflows with human-approval waits, retries and audit history.
- MLOps (GitLab) and AWS development/staging using de-identified data only.
- Observability and operations: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus + Grafana, ELK/Loki, model and agent monitoring, backup/DR and cost monitoring.

OAuth2/OIDC, SCIM, multi-tenancy, tenant isolation and Temporal are proposed design elements of this target architecture.
architectures.business_context: Target architecture for taking a credit-appraisal POC towards an enterprise-grade platform, with people approving every decision.
architectures.alt: Proposed banking AI copilot platform diagram with users and integrations, application layer, agent orchestration, workflow engine, MLOps and AWS staging, observability and an end-to-end flow

architectures.title: Hybrid Banking AI / MLOps — OpenStack Production + GitLab CI/CD + AWS SageMaker
architectures.summary: Credit-appraisal AI runs on a private OpenStack Kubernetes cluster; GitLab is the MLOps control plane; AWS SageMaker handles training, evaluation and a staging replica. Only approved, de-identified data moves to AWS.
architectures.description:
- Production (OpenStack / Kubernetes): FastAPI backend, a LangGraph credit-appraisal agent coordinating credit-scoring, asset-appraisal, legal and fraud agents, an MCP tool gateway, private Llama inference on vLLM, credit rules and approval by a credit officer, and decision write-back to core banking through Temenos APIs. Data layer: PostgreSQL + pgvector, Neo4j and Ceph object storage; Argo CD syncs approved releases.
- GitLab CI/CD: build, unit, security/compliance and integration tests, release quality gates, manual release approval, GitOps manifests and a private artifact repository.
- AWS: data preparation from de-identified cases, SageMaker Pipelines, fine-tuning (Llama / LoRA), evaluation and Model Registry, and an EKS/ECS staging replica monitored with CloudWatch.
architectures.business_context: Keeps customer data and live inference inside the bank’s private cloud while using AWS for experimentation, training and evaluation. Mirrors the hybrid banking design worked on at Rackspace; production deployment was outside the demonstrated POC.
architectures.alt: Hybrid architecture diagram: OpenStack production environment, GitLab CI/CD control plane and AWS SageMaker development and staging

architectures.title: Hybrid Banking AI / MLOps — OpenStack Production + GitLab CI/CD + Google Vertex AI
architectures.summary: The same hybrid pattern on Google Cloud: production inference stays on OpenStack while Vertex AI Pipelines, a model registry and a GKE staging replica support development and evaluation.
architectures.description:
- Production on OpenStack Kubernetes: FastAPI, a LangGraph credit-appraisal agent with specialist agents, MCP tool gateway, private Llama on vLLM, human approval by a credit officer and Temenos write-back.
- Data preparation on OpenStack, with de-identification validation (e.g. Presidio / ARX) before encrypted transfer of approved data to Cloud Storage.
- Vertex AI Pipelines for fine-tuning (Llama / LoRA), evaluation and model registry; staging on GKE / Cloud Run with vLLM, PostgreSQL + pgvector and Neo4j.
- GitLab CI/CD with quality gates and manual approval; Argo CD deploys approved releases back to OpenStack.
- A nine-step improvement cycle from production usage to monitoring and feedback.
architectures.business_context: An alternative to the AWS variant for organisations standardised on Google Cloud, with the same rule: only approved, de-identified datasets leave the private cloud.
architectures.alt: Hybrid architecture diagram: OpenStack production, GitLab CI/CD and Google Vertex AI development and staging, with a nine-step MLOps cycle

architectures.title: Continuous AI Improvement Workflow — OpenStack to AWS and Back
architectures.summary: A ten-step improvement loop that keeps live customer data on private OpenStack and moves only approved, de-identified datasets to AWS for training and staging.
architectures.description:
- Steps 1–3 on OpenStack: production usage and monitoring, selection of representative cases with human feedback and corrections, de-identification and data-quality validation.
- Steps 4–6 on AWS: encrypted transfer of approved data to S3, reproduction of the current baseline, Llama / LoRA fine-tuning and evaluation in SageMaker, and staging validation on EKS/ECS.
- Steps 7–8 in GitLab: automated tests, security and compliance checks, model evaluation review, human approval and release packaging into a private artifact store.
- Steps 9–10 back on OpenStack: GitOps deployment with Argo CD, canary/regression tests, RAG re-indexing, promote or roll back, and monitoring that feeds the next cycle.
architectures.business_context: Lets a regulated organisation improve its AI from real outcomes without moving live customer data out of its private cloud.
architectures.alt: Ten-step continuous AI improvement workflow between OpenStack production, AWS training and staging, and GitLab CI/CD

architectures.asset: Continuous AI Improvement Workflow on GCP.png
architectures.title: Continuous AI Improvement Workflow — OpenStack to Google Cloud and Back
architectures.summary: The ten-step improvement loop on Google Cloud: approved, anonymized data goes to Cloud Storage, Vertex AI trains and evaluates, GKE stages, and releases return to OpenStack.
architectures.description:
- On OpenStack: production usage and monitoring, case selection with human feedback, de-identification (e.g. Presidio / ARX) and data-quality approval.
- On Google Cloud: encrypted upload to Cloud Storage with IAM and VPC Service Controls, baseline reproduction, Llama / Gemini LoRA fine-tuning, RAG and agent evaluation in Vertex AI, and staging validation on GKE against business metrics.
- In GitLab: automated tests, security and compliance checks, model evaluation review, human approval and Helm release packages in Artifact Registry.
- Back on OpenStack: Argo CD GitOps sync, canary/regression tests, RAG re-indexing, promote or roll back, and monitoring for the next cycle.
architectures.business_context: Same principle as the AWS variant: live customer data stays private; only approved, de-identified or synthetic data is used for training.
architectures.alt: Ten-step continuous AI improvement workflow between OpenStack production, Google Cloud training and staging, and GitLab CI/CD

architectures.title: AWS MLOps Workflow with GitLab CI/CD
architectures.summary: End-to-end MLOps on AWS: governed data, SageMaker training and evaluation, GitLab CI/CD with security checks, staged rollout and monitored retraining — with no automatic promotion to production.
architectures.description:
- Data & model development: ingestion (AWS DMS, Kinesis) into a versioned S3 data lake governed with Glue Data Catalog and Lake Formation; validation with quarantine for failed quality checks; SageMaker Feature Store and time-aware train/validation/test splits; SageMaker Pipelines for training, tuning, evaluation on holdout data, a threshold gate and Model Registry.
- CI/CD & release control (GitLab): linting, unit, data-contract and integration tests; dependency, secrets, container and IaC scanning; signed images in Amazon ECR; pipeline triggers, evaluation results, staging tests, human approval and an immutable release manifest.
- Staging, deployment & monitoring: separate staging and production accounts, blue/green or canary rollout with rollback to the previous approved version, CloudWatch and SageMaker Model Monitor for drift and quality, EventBridge alerts, and a feedback loop that triggers candidate retraining — always with human approval.
architectures.business_context: A reference pattern for teams that need reproducible models, auditable releases and safe rollouts on AWS.
architectures.alt: AWS MLOps workflow diagram in three stages: data and model development, GitLab CI/CD and release control, staging, deployment and monitoring

architectures.title: Web Banking Application Architecture on AWS
architectures.summary: A secure, highly available internet-banking platform on AWS: edge protection, multi-AZ application and data tiers, hybrid connectivity to core banking, and built-in operations and security.
architectures.description:
- Customer access & edge: Route 53, CloudFront, AWS WAF and Shield, Certificate Manager and optional Cognito with MFA.
- Production VPC across two Availability Zones: Application Load Balancers, containerised web and API tiers (ECS / EKS / EC2) with auto scaling, Aurora and ElastiCache in private data subnets, plus S3, SQS, KMS, Secrets Manager and VPC endpoints.
- Hybrid connectivity: site-to-site VPN, Direct Connect or Transit Gateway to core banking and payment systems.
- Operations, security & delivery: CloudWatch, X-Ray, CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty and Security Hub; CodeCommit → CodeBuild → ECR → CodeDeploy; Systems Manager, AWS Backup, multi-region disaster recovery and cost optimisation.
architectures.business_context: Reference design for a bank’s customer-facing web and mobile channels: low latency, strong perimeter security and defined RTO/RPO.
architectures.alt: AWS web banking architecture: customer access and edge layer, multi-AZ production VPC, and operations, security and delivery

architectures.title: AI Credit Appraisal Workflow on Microsoft Azure
architectures.summary: Concept for AI-assisted rural micro-credit: farmers upload photos and documents, specialist agents analyse them, and a loan officer makes the final decision before core-banking integration.
architectures.description:
A ten-step workflow:
- Application intake through a farmer mobile app and a loan-officer portal
- OCR and document extraction (Azure AI Document Intelligence)
- Validation, enrichment and PII detection
- Knowledge retrieval with Azure AI Search and PostgreSQL + pgvector
- Specialist agents for credit scoring, asset appraisal, policy compliance and fraud/AML
- Financial calculations and scenario analysis
- An explainable recommendation with citations and risk flags
- Human review and decision by the loan officer, with a full audit trail
- System integration (API Management, Logic Apps, Service Bus) to create the customer record, loan account and disbursement workflow
- Continuous evaluation with Azure ML / MLflow and Azure Monitor

Security and identity use Microsoft Entra ID, Key Vault, private endpoints and Defender for Cloud.
architectures.business_context: Fairer, faster and explainable credit decisions for rural finance, with loan officers keeping decision authority.
architectures.alt: Azure AI credit appraisal workflow for rural finance: farmer app, loan officer portal, AI analysis, officer decision and core-banking integration

architectures.title: Cosmetics Supply Chain AI Copilot Platform (v2)
architectures.summary: Private, human-centred supply-chain AI for one factory, three warehouses and SAP S/4HANA: an agent hierarchy recommends, people approve, and SAP execution stays authorised and traceable.
architectures.description:
- SAP S/4HANA as the system of record (MM, PP, SD, QM; optional EWM/TM) behind a controlled integration layer: read-only for a POC, human-approved write-backs for production.
- Agent hierarchy: a cosmetics industry agent, a company supervisor agent (LangGraph + Flowise + MCP tool gateway), and factory-planning, procurement, warehouse, inventory-optimisation, logistics and quality/compliance agents.
- FastAPI / MCP tool gateway with schema validation, RBAC/ABAC permissions, an audit trail and human approval checkpoints — no unrestricted SAP writes.
- Private data and knowledge: S3 data lake, RDS PostgreSQL, vector RAG and an optional knowledge graph.
- Decision-outcome learning and private MLOps on SageMaker; optional, opt-in industry learning that shares only approved, anonymised derived artefacts.
architectures.business_context: Aims at better forecast accuracy, better stock balance with less waste, lower operating costs and improved supplier reliability — with people in control. These are design goals, not measured results.
architectures.contribution: Architecture design and documentation, building on the SAP supply-chain copilot designed at FPT Software.
architectures.alt: Cosmetics supply chain AI copilot platform: business flow, SAP S/4HANA environment, agent hierarchy, tool gateway with human-in-the-loop, private data layer and MLOps
